title: Torus fixed groups preserve surjections of connected affine algebraic groups
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $H,J$ be smooth connected affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-connected-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $R\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ be a torus, $r\geq0$, acting on both groups by group automorphisms, and let $q:H\to J$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism which is $R$-equivariant. For either group define its fixed subgroup functor by requiring invariance under all $R(V)$ after every further base change. The induced map $H^R\to J^R$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented, with scheme-theoretic kernel $(\ker q)^R$. Consequently $J^R$ is the fppf sheaf quotient $H^R/(\ker q)^R$. The kernel of $q$ need not be smooth or connected.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.5 proof, printed p.101: surjectivity on torus centralizers for surjections of smooth connected affine groups over a field. The scheme version uses the smooth fixed groups and the faithfully flat quotient map onto the group-theoretic image; it includes inseparable kernels. WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-normal-kernel-factorization] to $q$ and the acting group $R$. Obtain $q=b\circ a$, $a:H\to P=H/(\ker q)_{\mathrm{red}}$ a smooth quotient torsor and $b:P\to J$ finite faithfully flat radicial, all $R$-equivariant. The rank-zero torus is a smooth connected acting group too. By [lem-sfb-relative-torus-automorphism-fixed-group], $H^R,P^R,J^R$ are smooth connected affine groups of finite presentation; equivariance restricts $a,b$ to homomorphisms $a^R,b^R$.

source.place: Agent expansion of Conrad Corollary 3.3.5, printed p.101; Milne Algebraic Groups, Chapters 5, 10, 12, 13 and 17

proof.text: Put $L=(\ker q)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Apply [lem-sfb-homogeneous-cotangent-associated-bundle] to the smooth closed subgroup $L\subset H$ and its quotient torsor $a$. In particular $da_e:\operatorname{Lie}H\to\operatorname{Lie}P$ is surjective. Differentiating the equivariance identity makes this a homomorphism of rational $R$-representations. Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition] to both tangent spaces: for a weight-zero vector $w$ in the target, choose a lift $v=\sum_\chi v_\chi$. Equivariance and uniqueness of the weight decomposition give $da_e(v_0)=w$. Thus $da_e$ is surjective on invariant tangent spaces.

source.place: Agent expansion of Conrad Corollary 3.3.5, printed p.101; Milne Algebraic Groups, Chapters 5, 10, 12, 13 and 17

proof.text: For any one of the three groups $G$, a tangent vector of $G^R$ is a point $x\in G(k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$ reducing to $1$ and fixed under $R$ after every further algebra extension. Such an $x$ lies in $G^R$ exactly when its tangent vector in $\operatorname{Lie}G$ is invariant under the full differentiated $R$-action: substitute $k[\epsilon]$ into the defining universal fixed-point identity. Hence $\operatorname{Lie}(G^R)=(\operatorname{Lie}G)^R$, naturally for equivariant homomorphisms. Step 2 therefore says that $d(a^R)_e$ is surjective.

source.place: Agent expansion of Conrad Corollary 3.3.5, printed p.101; Milne Algebraic Groups, Chapters 5, 10, 12, 13 and 17

proof.text: Factor $a^R$ by [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] as $H^R\xrightarrow{u}I\xrightarrow{j}P^R$, where $u$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented and $j$ is a closed immersion. The source $H^R$ is smooth, so [lem-sbc-smooth-flat-surjective-source-descent] makes $I$ smooth over $k$. Since $d(a^R)_e=dj_e\circ du_e$ is surjective, $dj_e$ is surjective. The group $P^R$ is connected; [lem-sfb-smooth-subgroup-full-tangent] now gives $I=P^R$. Thus $a^R$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented.

source.place: Agent expansion of Conrad Corollary 3.3.5, printed p.101; Milne Algebraic Groups, Chapters 5, 10, 12, 13 and 17

proof.text: Let $y\in J^R(k)$. Finite faithful flatness and radiciality of $b$ give a unique $x\in P(k)$ with $b(x)=y$. For $t\in R(k)$, equivariance gives $b(t\cdot x)=t\cdot y=y$, so uniqueness gives $t\cdot x=x$. This equality holds as a morphism $R\to P$: $R$ is the spectrum of the reduced finitely generated Laurent polynomial algebra, and [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] applied to coordinate differences identifies the orbit morphism with the constant morphism at $x$. Consequently $x$ is fixed functorially after every algebra extension. We have proved $P^R(k)\to J^R(k)$ surjective; this uses no separability of $b$.

source.place: Agent expansion of Conrad Corollary 3.3.5, printed p.101; Milne Algebraic Groups, Chapters 5, 10, 12, 13 and 17

proof.text: Factor $b^R$ as $P^R\to I\hookrightarrow J^R$ by [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization]. Step 5 puts every $k$-point of $J^R$ in this closed image. The smooth affine group $J^R$ is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Its image ideal vanishes at every $k$-point, so [lem-wf-affine-nullstellensatz-vanishing] makes that ideal zero. Thus $I=J^R$ and $b^R$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented. Its composite with $a^R$ is $q^R$. Flatness of this composite is [lem-pc-flat-compose], surjectivity is composition of the underlying surjections, and finite presentation follows on affine coordinate rings from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](2).

source.place: Agent expansion of Conrad Corollary 3.3.5, printed p.101; Milne Algebraic Groups, Chapters 5, 10, 12, 13 and 17

proof.text: For every $k$-scheme $U$, the kernel of $q^R$ consists of the $h\in H(U)$ satisfying $q(h)=1$ and the universal $R$-fixed identity. These are exactly the points of $(\ker q)^R(U)$. This equality is natural in $U$, so it identifies the scheme-theoretic kernels, including nilpotents; no replacement of $\ker q$ by its reduction is made in this assertion.

source.place: Agent expansion of Conrad Corollary 3.3.5, printed p.101; Milne Algebraic Groups, Chapters 5, 10, 12, 13 and 17

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $q^R$. Its image factor is all of $J^R$, since $q^R$ is faithfully flat. The quotient clause of that node and step 7 identify $J^R$ with the fppf sheafification of $U\mapsto H^R(U)/(\ker q)^R(U)$, which is the asserted quotient.
